claims.explanation: AZD7762 is a CHK1/2 inhibitor that selectively kills tumor cells with a defective G1 DNA-damage checkpoint, most commonly through TP53 mutation or loss, forcing reliance on CHK1-mediated S/G2 arrest and homologous recombination repair; inhibiting CHK1 in these cells causes mitotic catastrophe and apoptosis. Additional sensitivity is conferred by defects in homologous recombination (BRCA1/2, ATM) or other DNA-repair/chromatin pathways, while intact p53 or certain oncogenic contexts (e.g., BRAF-mutant melanoma without p53 loss) are protective.

features.basis: Loss of G1 checkpoint creates dependence on CHK1; p53-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines and supported by literature
Homologous recombination deficiency impairs DNA repair, and CHK1 inhibition further blocks HR; BRCA1-mutant HCC1954 is sensitive
HR deficiency sensitizes to CHK1 inhibition; BRCA2-mutant LUDLU1 is sensitive
ATM loss impairs DNA damage signaling and repair, increasing reliance on CHK1; ATM-mutant 8305C is sensitive
Higher CHK1 expression may compensate for drug inhibition and reduce sensitivity
CDKN2A loss disrupts cell cycle control and DNA damage response, potentially increasing CHK1 dependence
RB1 loss deregulates G1/S checkpoint, increasing reliance on G2/M checkpoints; RB1-mutant FTC133 is sensitive
Chromatin remodeling defects may impair DNA repair; ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines
PI3K pathway activation may increase replication stress and CHK1 dependence; PIK3CA mutations enriched in sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines without p53 loss (e.g., SH4, IGR37) are less affected, suggesting BRAF-driven melanomas may not rely on CHK1
PTEN loss without p53 mutation (e.g., ZR751, 786O) is associated with less sensitivity, possibly via intact G1 checkpoint
ERBB3 mutations appear in sensitive lines (NCIH1792, SNUC5 is resistant though), weak evidence
